title: private-deployment-acme-weekly-sync-2026-03-16
content:
Weekly sync notes for ACME private deployment (VPC + on-prem) - prep and follow-ups

Date: 2026-03-16
Attendees (planned): Jordan Lee (owner), Maya Patel (SRE lead), Ethan Brooks (solutions eng), Sofia Kim (customer PM), Javier (ACME infra), ops on-call TBD
Channel: #acme-private-deploy (Slack) + this doc as scratchpad

Agenda (prep):
- Quick status: infra readiness, network config, firewall rules
- On-prem hardware ETA + rack scheduling
- VPC peering and route propagation issues (DEPLOY-412)
- KMS/HSM key provisioning and cert rotation plan
- Demo checklist for customer acceptance testing (CAT)
- Risks/blockers and owners + next steps

Current milestone map (short):
- Milestone A: VPC peering established + subnets approved (target: 2026-03-18) — MAYA/Ethan
- Milestone B: On-prem rack & GPU install complete (target: 2026-03-22) — ACME ops + Javier
- Milestone C: Private control plane deployed in staging + KMS integrated (target: 2026-03-25) — Jordan/Maya
- Milestone D: CAT and performance verification (target: 2026-03-29) — Ethan/Sofia

Open/blocking items (to surface):
- DEPLOY-412: BGP route leak between ACME VPC and our customer VPC peer — observed route flaps, causes transient connectivity loss. Blocker: ACME network team needs to confirm ASN config. Owner: Javier (ACME). Action: request outbound traceroutes from both sides, collect bgp table snapshots. (Jira: DEPLOY-412)
- HSM/KMS access: ACME security requires HSM-backed keys; their KMS vendor has specific cert rotation schedule that conflicts with our current bootstrap script (scripts use short TTL). Owner: Jordan. Blocker: need vendor rotation window and new bootstrap approach.
- Rack scheduling: On-prem vendor pushed ETA by 2 days due to shipment delay. Impact: pushes Milestone B to 2026-03-24 unless we get earlier slot. Owner: Sofia to escalate with ACME procurement.
- Monitoring alerts: Prometheus scraping of on-prem nodes failing intermittently (auth errors). Owner: Maya. Hypothesis: DNS resolution for control-plane endpoints sometimes returns old IP from local cache. Need repro steps.

Notes / talking points for the call:
- Start with quick wins: show VPC peering status and that we have BGP community tags in place (pre-empt DEPLOY-412 concerns)
- Ask ACME for ASN confirmation and router config snapshot (explicit request)
- Walk through KMS requirement: outline two options (1) accept vendor rotation window and adjust bootstrap TTLs, (2) run temporary soft-keys until HSM rollout complete — pros/cons and security signoff needed
- Confirm acceptance criteria for CAT: 99% p95 latency < 500ms for 1k qps (simulated), auth/audit logs accessible in SIEM, and zero data egress to public networks

Action items (explicit follow-ups):
- Jordan: Draft KMS bootstrap patch that supports vendor rotation (ETA: 2026-03-18) — link: github.com/redwood-inference/acme-deployments/pull/87
- Maya: Collect Prometheus scrape logs and DNS cache traces from on-prem node 3 and share in #acme-private-deploy (ETA: 2026-03-17)
- Sofia: Escalate rack shipment with ACME procurement and confirm new ETA by EOD 2026-03-17
- Javier (ACME): Provide BGP config snapshot and ASN confirmation; run traceroute from ACME edge to our peer (ETA: 2026-03-17)
- Ethan: Prepare CAT perf test harness and baseline numbers for previous week to show trend (ETA: 2026-03-19)
- All: Add any missing acceptance bullets to the CAT checklist in Confluence (link above) before next sync
- Jordan/Maya: Plan short-run fallback: if on-prem not ready by 2026-03-24, provision temporary dedicated hosted capacity to run CAT (cost estimate to share)

Risks to call out:
- KMS vendor rotation mismatch could block control-plane start if not addressed quickly
- Persistent BGP flaps might require a maintenance window with ACME network — could delay CAT by multiple days
- On-prem hardware delays create sequencing risk for integration testing (we may need to shuffle staging->prod swap)

Notes to self (scratch):
- Bring up DEPLOY-412 early, but avoid finger-pointing. Offer to run the traceroutes and analyze BGP dumps ourselves if ACME is short-handed.
- Remember to ask whether ACME wants us to run initial performance tests outside their SIEM ingestion window to avoid noise on their dashboards
- Confirm who is taking notes on ACME side during the meeting (Sofia said maybe Javier?)

Next sync: 2026-03-23 10:00 PT (propose) — confirm with ACME in today's thread.

Quick link roundup for attendees:
- Jira: https://jira.redwood.ai/browse/DEPLOY-412
- Confluence runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ACME/ACME+Private+Deployment+Runbook
- PR (KMS bootstrap): github.com/redwood-inference/acme-deployments/pull/87

End of notes.

(Informal, leave as working doc — will tidy into runbook if items stabilize)
